checks.title: Entry-timing difference is declared
checks.detail: kernel enters at the hourly close; the live bot scans every 5 min on a forming candle, so the kernel reads pumps +0.54pp larger on average (188 matched setups). DECLARED LIMITATION: arena absolute WR is not live WR. Arm-vs-arm comparisons stay valid — all arms share this kernel — but a promoted arm must still survive the earlier live entry, and that caveat is attached to every surfaced verdict.

findings.claim: STATISTICAL REALITY: 'measured ghost arrival = 25.6 control trades/day', used to make confirm n=600 look reachable.
findings.problem: Nothing in the live tape supports that rate. Events by tier show live=25 total, and control has taken only 8 live trades in the whole window (live_n=4 resolved plus 4 still open, declined=17). 25.6/day is a backfill-derived arrival rate presented as 'measured'; at the actual live rate, n=600 per arm is not a schedule this arena can reach, and every 'confirm' stage label rests on that unstated substitution.

findings.claim: Checklist arms_running is green — '5 running: tp-7pct, hold-12h, entry-8pct, sl-5pct, vol-4x' — and all seven arms are labelled [running/confirm].
findings.problem: The check establishes registration, not evidence accumulation. Live samples are live_n=1 (entry-8pct), 2 (vol-4x), 3 (sl-5pct, tp-7pct), 4 (control, hold-12h, placebo) against a planned confirm n=600. Every quoted screen_wr, screen_ev and screen_dWR comes from the backfill tier (4764 backfill events vs 25 live), so an arm shown as 'running/confirm' with a 5.26pp dWR is carrying a backfill verdict under a live-stage label — exactly the META failure mode the project already recorded as G-37.

findings.claim: entry_granularity_declared: 'Arm-vs-arm comparisons stay valid — all arms share this kernel.'
findings.problem: Shared bias only cancels when the bias is orthogonal to the arm's parameter. The declared kernel bias is that pumps read +0.54pp larger on 188 matched setups; entry-8pct's only change is pump_pct=8.0, i.e. a threshold on the exact quantity that is mis-measured. Its screen_n=494 is therefore a different selected population than pump_pct=8.0 would produce live, and no equivalent caveat is attached to it. This is a PM risk that the green checkbox actively declares away.

findings.claim: paired_population is green: '4789 events in the shared window; every arm has seen all of them.'
findings.problem: Seeing the same detections is not being scored on the same events. Scored counts differ — control 1541, sl-5pct 1540, tp-7pct 1540 — and the excluded open trades are arm-dependent (control 4, sl-5pct 5, tp-7pct 5, entry-8pct 1, vol-4x 3). Exit-parameter arms resolve on different clocks, so censoring is differential by construction: the paired dWR figures (sl-5pct 5.26pp, hold-12h 3.18pp) are computed over sets that are not identical, and the check's wording hides that.

findings.claim: backfill_cannot_promote is green: '0 surfaced arm(s); none promoted from a screen.'
findings.problem: The check passes vacuously. With zero arms ever surfaced, no promotion path has been exercised, so the result is consistent both with a working gate and with a gate that has never executed. A green critical checkbox that cannot distinguish those two states does not establish the property it names, and it will keep reading green until the first promotion — the moment it stops being informative.

findings.claim: Arena reports sl-5pct at screen_wr=55.195, screen_dWR=5.26pp — the largest win-rate delta on the board.
findings.problem: The objective is win rate AND EV per trade, but sl-5pct's screen_ev=0.022 is below control's 0.029 on the same window, so the headline delta is presented while the arm is losing on the other half of the stated objective. No paired p-value or discordant-pair count is reported for any dWR against the corrected alpha=0.00833, even though the project's own L-sl-entry-anchor kill did report them (p=9.18e-41, b=0/c=134). A dWR quoted without its paired test is a max-of-k selection waiting to happen (MT).
